AWARD/JUDGMENT 1.

The present Detailed Accident Report (DAR) for compensation relates to grievous injury and permanent disability suffered by the claimant Sh. Kamal Ram in a road accident that took place on 23.08.2018 at around 02:33 PM, infront of G Block Bus Stand, K Kamraj Marg, New Delhi,
regarding which one FIR No.43/18, U/s 279/338 IPC was registered at PS South Avenue.

The vehicle involved in this case is a motorcycle bearing registration No. DL-3SAG-3600, which at the relevant time of accident was being driven by respondent no.1 (R1) Sh. Pradeep Kumar and owned by respondent no. 2 Sh. Sharan Veer Singh.
2. It is the case of the claimant that he is employed with Delhi Police as a Head Constable.
On 23.08.2018, he was deployed at Ex-PM Cell, Vinay Marg, Security Lines.
On that day, he was travelling in a bus (route no. 780) from Vinay Marg, Security Lines and got down at G Block, Bus Stand at K. Kamraj Marg.

At about 2:30 pm, when the claimant was crossing K. Kamraj Marg towards Udyog Bhawan Metro Station, all of a sudden, the offending vehicle bearing registration No.
DL-3SAG-3600, which was being driven by respondent no. 1 at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, came from circle crossing of K. Kamraj Marg and hit the claimant due to which Kamal Ram vs Pradeep Kumar on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18113031/

he sustained grievous injuries.
He was removed to Dr. RML Hospital where his MLC was prepared by the doctors.

3. Respondents no. 1 and 2 have filed their written statement/reply to the DAR wherein it is submitted that the respondent no. 1 was driving his motorcycle on the correct side of the road and at a normal speed.
It is further submitted that the claimant himself was negligent while crossing the road.
When R-1 reached infront of G Block bus stand near K. Kamraj Marg, New Delhi, the injured/claimant suddenly came on the road passing from the front side of the bus.
It is further submitted that they were falsely implicated by the police in the present matter.

The Tribunal heard the arguments advanced by Sh. Manoj Bhandari Ld. Counsel for claimant and Sh. Bhushan Pawar and Sh. Zainul Abedeen, Ld. Counsels for R-1 and R-2 and has carefully perused the entire case record along with written submissions filed on behalf of claimant and R-1 & R-2.
The findings on the aforementioned issues are rendered hereinafter in the succeeding paragraphs.

1. Whether the injured Kamal Ram sustained injuries in the accident which occurred on 23.08.2018 at about 02:33 PM, infront of G Block Bus Stand, K Kamraj Marg, New Delhi caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle No. DL-3SAG-3600 being driven by respondent no.1 and owned by respondent no. 2 ? 11. Onus to prove this issue was upon the claimant.

The first question that needs to be decided is whether the accident was caused by the vehicle bearing registration No. DL-3SAG-3600.
12.
In order to prove the same, the claimant has examined himself as PW3.

In his evidence by way of affidavit Ex. PW3/A, he narrated the manner of accident as follows :-
"2.
That the deponent is employed with Delhi Police as a Head Constable and on 23.08.2018 was deployed as Ex-PM Cell, Vinay Marg, Security Lines.

On 23.08.2018,
deponent was travelling in a bus route no. 780 from Vinay Marg, Security Lines and got down at G-Block, Bus Stand at K. Kamraj Marg.

At about 2.30 pm as the deponent was crossing K. Kamraj Marg towards Udyog Bhawan Metro Station, then suddenly a motorcycle, bearing registration No. DL-3SAG-3600, which was being driven by respondent no. 1, coming from circle crossing of K. Kamraj Marg at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, without observing the traffic rules, could not control his motorcycle and rammed into/had hit very badly to the deponent,
which resulted in grievous injuries to the deponent."
13. During cross examination, PW1 deposed that he was crossing the road to go towards metro station and there was no zebra crossing.
He further deposed that there was no traffic on the road at the time of accident.
He denied the suggestion that the accident took place on account of his own negligence.
14. Respondent no. 1 examined himself as R1W1.

In his evidence by way of affidavit Ex. R1W1/A, he narrated the manner of accident as follows :-
"3.

That on 23.08.2018, the deponent was driving on the correct side of the road at a very normal speed and suddenly the injured came infront of the motorcycle of the R-1, it is pertinent to mention here that the injured was crossing the road from the part of the road where no zebra crossing was made in order to cross the road for pedestrians."

15. During cross examination, he admitted that the motorcycle bearing registration No.
DL-3SAG-3600 was not insured on the date of accident.
He further admitted that he was not holding a valid and effective driving license to drive the motorcycle at the time of accident.

16. As per the DAR/chargesheet, the accident in question took place because of rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing registration no. DL-3SAG-3600.

sentences.text: It has been further observed that even when the accused were to be acquitted in the criminal case, the same may be of no effect on the assessment of the liability required in respect of motor accident cases by the Tribunal.

19. It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a Civil Court and in Civil matters, the facts are required to be established on preponderance of probabilities and not beyond reasonable doubt, as are required in a criminal prosecution.

Reference in this regard is made to the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court reported as (2009) 13 SC 530 in Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others,
wherein it has been observed that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants and the claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.

In view of foregoing discussion, it stands proved on preponderance of probability that the aforesaid accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing registration no. DL-3SAG-3600 and the said vehicle at that time was driven by respondent no. 1 and owned by respondent no.2.
Hence, this issue is decided in favour of the claimant and against the respondents.
21. ISSUE NO.2 2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

22.

sentences.text: In terms of Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, the compensation which is to be awarded by this Tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In injury cases, a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensation i.e. pecuniary as well as non- pecuniary damages.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343, has laid down heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases as:-
Pecuniary damages (Special Damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising :
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment;
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.

entities.text: Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (iii) Future medical expenses.
Non-pecuniary damages (General Damages)
(iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage).

(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
24.

Having considered the ratio of aforesaid judgment, the compensation payable to claimant is assessed hereinafter under the following heads as:-
(i) Medical or Treatment Expenses 25.

PW3 has tendered on record copy of his discharge summary issued as Ex. PW3/12, as per which the claimant was initially admitted in Dr. RML Hospital on 23.08.2018 and was discharged on the same day where his MLC was prepared and he was diagnosed with fracture both bone leg right,
fracture distal and radius and ulna.

Thereafter, the claimant was admitted in Cygnus MLS Hospital,
Delhi for further treatment on 23.08.2018 and was discharged on 27.08.2018 where he was diagnosed with segmental fracture tibia right with fibula fracture right and had undergone various operative procedures.
26. PW1 in his examination in chief has deposed that as per record, the claimant has not taken any medical reimbursement from Security Unit.
However, he has availed credit facility (cashless) on the medical bills dated 17.09.2018 for a sum of Rs.1,31,443/- and medical bill dated 26.03.2019 for a sum of Rs.13,299/- in the Cygnus Hospital.

The respondents have failed to lead any evidence to show that the said medical bills do not relate to the injuries suffered by the claimant in the aforesaid accident.
Thus, the testimony of PW-1 that he had spent the aforesaid amount towards medical expenses remained unrebutted and uncontroverted.
In the absence of any plausible evidence produced by respondents on record, there is no reason to disbelieve the testimony of PW-1 that he had spent the aforesaid amount towards medical expenses.
Hence, he is held entitled to Rs.40,585/- towards his medical expenses.
(ii) Loss of earnings 28.
The claimant in his affidavit Ex. PW3/A has claimed that he is employed as Head Constable with Delhi Police and was getting salary of Rs.63,133/- per month.

He has tendered on record copy of his ID card issued by Delhi Police as Ex. PW3/1 and copy of salary slip for the month of August, 2018 as Ex. PW3/15.

30.

Perusal of attested copy of salary slip of claimant for the month of August, 2018 reflects his gross salary as Rs.63,133/- per month, which is also apparent from the salary statement w.e.f. April 2018 to October 2021 as Ex. PW1/1 (colly) (OSR).

Record shows that as Head Constable of Delhi Police,
he received salary of 13 months in a year.
The thirteenth month salary constituted of Basic pay and DA.

Further, as per salary statement for the financial year 2018-19, which is part of Ex. PW1/1 (colly) (OSR), the gross annual salary of claimant is found recorded as Rs.8,10,707/- (salary equivalent to 13 months received in a year) and income tax to the tune of Rs.28,022/- was deducted.
Accordingly, after deducting the tax amount, the annual gross salary of claimant comes out to be Rs.7,82,685/- (Rs.8,10,707/- - Rs.28,022/-).

Hence, the net monthly salary/emoluments of claimant after deducting tax comes out to be Rs.65,224/- (rounded off) (Rs.7,82,685/12).
31
. PW3 in his affidavit has claimed that he remained on leave from his duty for a period of 316 days due to the injuries sustained in the accident.

He deposed that the claimant remained on leave for a total period of 316 days, i.e. medical commuted leave for a period of 189 days w.e.f. 23.08.2018 to 27.02.2019 and earned leave for a period of 127 days w.e.f. 28.02.2019 to 30.06.2019.

(iii) Loss of future earnings 36.

As per disability certificate issued by Dr. RML Hospital Ex. PW3/14, the claimant is a case of fracture of right tibia with fracture right radius, all fractures are united and his permanent physical disability is 10% in relation to right lower limb.
37.

The law with regard to grant of compensation due to permanent disability and determination of functional disability etc. was well settled by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Raj Kumar Vs.
Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343, wherein it has been held as under :-
"4.

Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343

sentences.text: The provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (`Act' for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.

(See C. K. Subramonia Iyer vs. T. Kunhikuttan Nair - AIR 1970 SC 376, R. D.
Hattangadi vs. Pest Control (India) Ltd. - 1995 (1) SCC 551 and Baker vs. Willoughby - 1970 AC 467).

entities.text: C. K. Subramonia Iyer vs. T. Kunhikuttan Nair - AIR 1970 SC 376

sentences.text: 10. Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps.

The Tribunal has to first ascertain what activities the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of the permanent ability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident, as also his age.

The third step is to find out whether (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any Kamal Ram vs Pradeep Kumar on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18113031/
7 kind of livelihood, or (ii) whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (iii) whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions, but could carry on some other or lesser scale of activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood.
For example, if the left hand of a claimant is amputated, the permanent physical or functional disablement may be assessed around 60%.
If the claimant was a driver or a carpenter, the actual loss of earning capacity may virtually be hundred percent, if he is neither able to drive or do carpentry.

On the other hand, if the claimant was a clerk in government service, the loss of his left hand may not result in loss of employment and he may still be continued as a clerk as he could perform his clerical functions; and in that event the loss of earning capacity will not be 100% as in the case of a driver or carpenter, nor 60% which is the actual physical disability, but far less.

In fact, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of `loss of future earnings', if the claimant continues in government service,
though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities as a consequence of losing his hand.

Sometimes the injured claimant may be continued in service, but may not found suitable for discharging the duties attached to the post or job which he was earlier holding, on account of his disability, and may therefore be shifted to some other suitable but lesser post with lesser emoluments, in which case there should be a limited award under the head of loss of future earning capacity,
taking note of the reduced earning capacity.

It may be noted that when compensation is awarded by treating the loss of future earning capacity as 100% (or even anything more than 50%), the need to award compensation separately under the head of loss of amenities or loss of expectation of life may disappear and as a result, only a token or nominal amount may have to be awarded under the head of loss of amenities or loss of expectation of life, as otherwise there may be a duplication in the award of compensation.
Be that as it may............."

38. Coming back to the present matter, the claimant was working as Head Constable with Delhi Police and the said disability would certainly affect the efficiency of claimant in doing his job,
specifically, field job.

Considering the legal position discussed above coupled with the testimony of PW3, his profession and his age, the functional disability of claimant is, therefore, taken as 5% in relation to whole body.
39. To apply the multiplier, it is necessary to ascertain the age of the claimant.
The claimant has tendered on record copy of his Aadhaar card as Mark A in which the date of birth is mentioned as 20.08.1968.
Hence, going by these documents, the age of claimant comes out to be 50 years and 3 days at the time of accident.

Therefore, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr., (2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Apex Court in a judgment of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors., SLP (Civil) No. 25590 of 2014 dated 31.10.2017,
the multiplier of '13' is applicable for calculating the loss of future earnings of the claimant arising out of above disability.

Thus, the loss of future earnings caused to the claimant due to his permanent disability comes to Rs.6,61,371/- (rounded off) (Rs.65,224/- X 12 X 5/100 X 13 X 130/100).
(iv) Mental and Physical Shock, Pain and Sufferings & Loss of Amenities 41.
As stated above, the claimant had suffered grievous injuries and permanent disability in the accident.

Though, it is not possible to exactly compensate him for the shock, pain and sufferings etc.
which he had actually suffered because of the above injuries, but an effort has to be made to compensate him for the same in a just and reasonable manner.

Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by the claimant and duration of the treatment taken by him etc.,
an amount of Rs.50,000/- each is being awarded to him towards (i) mental and physical shock and (ii) for pain and sufferings respectively.
Further, an amount of Rs.25,000/- is also awarded to him towards the loss of amenities suffered by him during said period of his treatment.
Thus, he is awarded total amount of Rs.1,25,000/- under this head.
(v) Conveyance, Special Diet and Attendant Charges 42.
The claimant in his affidavit has claimed that he had spent a sum of Rs. 50,000/- on special diet and Rs. 20,000/- towards conveyance.
However, he has not placed on record any document in order to substantiate his above claim.

Still this Tribunal can very well take note of the requirement of conveyance for claimant for frequently visiting the hospitals and doctors in connection with his treatment and special diet for his early recovery from the injuries suffered because of the accident.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the present case, an amount of Rs.15,000/- is being awarded to the claimant towards conveyance and Rs.25,000/- towards special diet.
43. The claimant in his affidavit has claimed that he has spent an amount of Rs. 60,000/- towards attendant charges.
Keeping in view the nature of injuries and disability suffered by the claimant, he would have required assistance of some family member/attendant for doing his daily routine work

,
therefore, a sum of Rs.60,000/- is also being awarded to the claimant towards attendant charges.

The claimant is thus entitled to an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rs.15,000/- + Rs. 25,000/- + Rs.
60,000/-) under this head.
ISSUE No. 3/Relief 44.

In view of foregoing discussion, the claimant is thus awarded a sum of Rs.16,13,982/- (Rupees Sixteen Lakh Thirteen Thousand Nine Hundred Eighty Two only) (Rs.40,585/- + Rs.6,87,026/- +
Rs.6,61,371/- + Rs.1,25,000/- + Rs.1,00,000/-) along with 7.5% interest from the date of filing of DAR.
However, it is directed that the amount of interim award and interest for the suspended period, if any, during the course of this inquiry, shall be liable to be excluded from the award amount.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Reliance is being placed upon the judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in case Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd.
Vs. Meera Devi & ors., 2021 LawSuit (Del) 2021 wherein it was held that "......in view of Delhi Motor Accident Claim Tribunal Rules, 2008, contents of DAR has to be presumed to be correct and read in evidence without formal proof of the same unless proof to the contrary was produced."
18. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303 has observed that filing of charge sheet against the driver prima facie points towards his complicity in driving the vehicle rashly and negligently.
It has been further observed that even when the accused were to be acquitted in the criminal case, the same may be of no effect on the assessment of the liability required in respect of motor accident cases by the Tribunal.
19. It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a Civil Court and in Civil matters, the facts are required to be established on preponderance of probabilities and not beyond reasonable doubt, as are required in a criminal prosecution.
Reference in this regard is made to the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court reported as (2009) 13 SC 530 in Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others,
wherein it has been observed that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants and the claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
In terms of Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, the compensation which is to be awarded by this Tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In injury cases, a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensation i.e. pecuniary as well as non- pecuniary damages.
Hence, the net monthly salary/emoluments of claimant after deducting tax comes out to be Rs.65,224/- (rounded off) (Rs.7,82,685/12).
31
Perusal of medical bills of claimant reflects that the claimant had taken treatment till the year 2021.
33.
It is explicit from the testimony of PW2 coupled with exhibited documents that the claimant had availed leaves for a total period of 316 days due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
In terms of the judgment dated 04.09.2012 given by the Hon'ble Delhi High Court in case of Sandeep Mishra Vs. Vijay Kumar Yadav & Ors., MAC App. No.215/2010, the petitioner is entitled to be compensated for all those leaves availed by him due to above accident irrespective of the nature of these leaves as it is now well settled that even if the leaves were paid leaves, the petitioner is entitled to be reimbursed for the same as he could have enjoyed or availed his leaves later on for his enjoyment or for enjoyment of his family members.
35. In view of aforesaid Judgment, this Tribunal feels it just and reasonable to compensate him for loss of earning equivalent to a period of 316 days.
The law with regard to grant of compensation due to permanent disability and determination of functional disability etc. was well settled by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Raj Kumar Vs.
Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343, wherein it has been held as under :-
"4.
(See C. K. Subramonia Iyer vs. T. Kunhikuttan Nair - AIR 1970 SC 376, R. D.
Hattangadi vs. Pest Control (India) Ltd. - 1995 (1) SCC 551 and Baker vs. Willoughby - 1970 AC 467).
The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident, as also his age.
Considering the legal position discussed above coupled with the testimony of PW3, his profession and his age, the functional disability of claimant is, therefore, taken as 5% in relation to whole body.
39. To apply the multiplier, it is necessary to ascertain the age of the claimant.
Hence, going by these documents, the age of claimant comes out to be 50 years and 3 days at the time of accident.
Therefore, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr., (2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Apex Court in a judgment of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors., SLP (Civil) No. 25590 of 2014 dated 31.10.2017,
the multiplier of '13' is applicable for calculating the loss of future earnings of the claimant arising out of above disability.

8 40.
Thus, the loss of future earnings caused to the claimant due to his permanent disability comes to Rs.6,61,371/- (rounded off) (Rs.65,224/- X 12 X 5/100 X 13 X 130/100).
As stated above, the claimant had suffered grievous injuries and permanent disability in the accident.
Though, it is not possible to exactly compensate him for the shock, pain and sufferings etc.
which he had actually suffered because of the above injuries, but an effort has to be made to compensate him for the same in a just and reasonable manner.
Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by the claimant and duration of the treatment taken by him etc.,
an amount of Rs.50,000/- each is being awarded to him towards (i) mental and physical shock and (ii) for pain and sufferings respectively.
Further, an amount of Rs.25,000/- is also awarded to him towards the loss of amenities suffered by him during said period of his treatment.
